title: Deadlines and written communication
detail: Key dates, review cycles and drafting practice

blocks.text: Dates specified in the supplied source Regulation, published on 18 December 2023

Separate initial implementation dates, recurring duties and incident-triggered deadlines. A deadline that is already past does not establish that the obligation was actually fulfilled. These notes retain the examination source’s dates without adding subsequent implementation measures.

rows: IICB guidelines or recommendations on incident-reporting arrangements, format and content: Article 21(9).
IICB implementation guidelines for the initial review, Framework, maturity, measures and plan: Article 5.

First annual IICB report to Parliament and Council: Article 10(14); report to the Commission with CERT-EU assistance: Article 25(1); incident-coordination guidelines or recommendations: Article 22(4).
Entity Framework after initial review: Article 6(1).
Entity risk-management measures, without undue delay and by this date at the latest: Article 8(1).
Management approval of the entity’s plan, without undue delay and by this date at the latest: Article 9(1).
First Commission evaluation and report to Parliament and Council on implementation and strategic and operational experience; includes considering CERT-EU’s possible Union-body status: Article 25(2).

Commission review of how the Regulation functions, including possible inclusion of EU classified systems, with reports to Parliament, Council, EESC and Committee of the Regions; legislative proposal where necessary: Article 25(3).

blocks.text: Budget and legal effect — Articles 24–26, page 27

The Commission may propose reallocating staff and financial resources to its budget for CERT-EU activities, taking effect with the first annual Union budget adopted after entry into force. The Regulation enters into force on the twentieth day after publication and is binding in its entirety and directly applicable in all Member States.

Regularly and at least every 5 years

IICB reporting under Articles 10(14) and 25(1); Head’s documents and reporting under Article 15; entity expert lists under Article 23(4).

blocks.text: The Framework establishes governance and policies. The entity’s cybersecurity plan includes its measures and individual crisis plan. The common IICB crisis plan organises coordinated management of major incidents. Articles 6, 9 and 23.

blocks.text: Competition notice EPSO/AD/429/26, section 4.3.2(d), page 9; drafting approach below is a practice suggestion

The EUFTE assesses written communication, lasts 40 minutes, is taken in language 2 and is marked out of 10 with a pass score of 5. The published documentation is available during the test with the assignment. It is neither a language test nor a factual-knowledge test. The notice refers to EPSO’s assessment anchors rather than reproducing them.

For every obligation, ask: who acts, what must be done, by when, and subject to which conditions or exceptions? Select information relevant to the assignment rather than reciting every module. Keep “shall”, “may”, “recommend”, “propose” and “adopt” distinct, and check the exact incident category.

A suggested 40-minute practice allocation is: five minutes to analyse the task, seven to select information and plan, twenty-one to draft, and seven to review. This is not an official EPSO prescription. In the review, check the actor, legal force, deadline starting point and any qualification.

For a broad synthesis, a possible structure is: 1. entity responsibility and preparedness; 2. common governance and support; 3. information sharing, reporting and coordinated crises, with safeguards. Adapt the introduction, headings and conclusion to the actual recipient and task.

rows: Each Union entity is required to…

blocks.question: Is maturity assessed every four years?
blocks.answer: No. At least every two years. Four years concerns the Framework review.

blocks.question: What are the four initial entity milestones?
blocks.answer: Framework in April twenty twenty-five, maturity in July, measures in September and the plan in January twenty twenty-six, each with the eighth of the month as its specified date.

blocks.question: Does the 2029 review already bring EU classified systems into the general scope?
blocks.answer: No. It assesses whether their inclusion is appropriate. Article 25(3).

blocks.question: Which four questions help you summarise an obligation?
blocks.answer: Who acts, what action is required, by when, and subject to which conditions or exceptions.

blocks.text: Draft a short briefing explaining the difference between the Framework, the entity plan and the common crisis plan. Then check the terminology and deadlines against the source. Practice task only.
